prompt:
You read a student's answer to a question about a short Java program and decide which rules the answer engages with.

Program:
% java RandomSeq 5 > data.txt
% java Average < data.txt
% java RandomSeq 5 | java Average
(RandomSeq N prints N random numbers; Average reads numbers from standard input and prints their average)

Question: What appears in the terminal after each command? What does args[] contain when Average runs?

Student's answer: "1: nothing, the numbers go into data.txt. 2: the average. 3: an average of 5 new numbers, no file. args is empty."

Concept under consideration: standard_input

Candidate edges of this concept. A misconception/error edge shows the wrong rule (logic) and the right rule (twin_logic); a concept edge shows the rule that links the two concepts; a level way (lvl:) shows one way an answer can display a level of understanding of the concept.
- lvl:standard_input@L0#0 | level L0 way everyday_reading: In everyday reading of `INPUT A` or `readInt`, the command looks like it inputs the letter A, or 'looks at' a number without using it up. In fact a read takes the next token from the input stream, converts it, and returns the value, which the program must store (e.g. int a = StdIn.readInt()).
- lvl:standard_input@L0#3 | level L0 way inconsistent_trace: Points to LT (each call blocks, then consumes exactly one token, in order). An uneven trace gives a variable a value that was already consumed, skips a token on some reads, or merges two READs into one. (here mixing in: "Calling StdIn.readInt() twice returns the same value twice")
- lvl:standard_input@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: StdIn is a booksite library of static methods that read typed values from the standard input stream: isEmpty, readInt, readDouble, readLong, readBoolean, readChar, readString, readLine, readAll.
- lvl:standard_input@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: StdIn reads from a stream that may be empty or may contain values separated by whitespace. readInt() reads the next token, parses it as an int and returns it, and the token must have the type the method expects. Outside the book's StdIn library, standard Java reads keyboard input with java.util.Scanner (nextInt(), nextDouble(), nextLine()); a token of the wrong type stops the program with InputMismatchException.
- lvl:standard_input@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: When execution reaches a read, the program blocks until a complete token is available (at the terminal, until <return>). The read then parses the token and returns, the assignment stores the value, and the next statement runs.
- lvl:standard_input@L2#1 | level L2 way output_prediction: readInt returns an int, readDouble a double, readString a String, readBoolean a boolean. AddInts 4 with input 144 233 377 1024 prints Sum is 1778.
- lvl:standard_input@L2#2 | level L2 way one_step_execution: One read moves the input position past one token and returns its value. Assigning that value overwrites the variable's previous value. No other variable changes.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#0 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: Every StdIn call takes from the same stream position, so values are delivered once, in order.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#1 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: To read an unknown number of values, each read must be guarded by !StdIn.isEmpty() as the condition of a while loop whose body reads.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#10 | level L3 way purpose_of_the_whole: StdIn brings an unbounded amount of data into a running program. The variable that receives each read plays the Sajaniemi role of most-recent holder.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#2 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: With `< file` the same StdIn calls read from the file instead of the keyboard. The program text does not change.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#3 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The reads must follow the file's layout: one readInt() for n first, then pairs of readInt() for each link i j until isEmpty().
- lvl:standard_input@L3#4 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The program turns the input stream into the output stream: values read with StdIn are processed and the results are written with StdOut. The two streams are independent.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#5 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: StdIn values can drive StdDraw output. PlotFilter reads x, y pairs and draws a point for each, after scaling from the first four numbers.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#6 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The method called fixes the type the next token must have: readInt needs an int literal, and readDouble accepts 5 or 5.0.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#7 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: Because a read can run at any point in execution, a read inside a loop lets each typed value decide the next branch.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#8 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: Token reads (readInt, readString) and line reads (readLine) share one position. A token read leaves the rest of its line for the next readLine, so it is best not to mix the two.
- lvl:standard_input@L3#9 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: Command-line arguments are a fixed number of strings given once when the program starts (args[]); standard input is a stream of any length read while the program runs (StdIn.readInt()). Both arrive as text and must be parsed into numbers.
- lvl:standard_input@L4#0 | level L4 way predict_a_change: Changing the input data changes the results without recompiling. Swapping two reads swaps the values the two variables get. Changing readInt to readDouble accepts more inputs; the reverse breaks on tokens like 12.2.
- lvl:standard_input@L4#1 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: StdIn/StdOut/StdDraw/StdAudio are not part of Java; their files must be in the working directory or on the classpath. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: StdIn.class is absent when the program runs: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: StdIn. If StdIn.java is absent when compiling, javac reports 'cannot find symbol' instead.
- lvl:standard_input@L4#2 | level L4 way transfer_to_a_new_program: Use StdIn when the amount of data is large or unknown, comes from a file or another program, or must be supplied while the program runs. Use command-line arguments for a few parameters fixed at launch.
- lvl:standard_input@L4#3 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: The next token must parse as the requested type. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: The next token is not an int literal, e.g. abc, 12.2 or true for readInt(). StdIn throws NumberFormatException in the book's version and InputMismatchException in the booksite/Scanner version.
- lvl:standard_input@L4#4 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: A read requires a remaining value; test StdIn.isEmpty() first. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: More reads than values: a fixed-count loop with too few inputs, or an unguarded read after EOF.
